subject: Acme: vulnerability closure artifacts and compensating controls
messages:
From: Claire Tremblay <claire.t@acmecorp.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Security Team <security@acmecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 01 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request for closure artifacts and compensating controls - Acme pentest findings

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We completed our initial review of the redacted pentest report you shared (reference attached to the portal). Before we close the items on our side, the security team needs concrete artifacts showing the corrective actions for the high and medium findings. Specifically for the items scoped to Redwood: 

- Finding 2: Insecure ACL on S3 artifact bucket (high) — we need a screenshot of the S3 console showing the new ACL/policy and a config snip of the applied bucket policy.
- Finding 4: Unescaped user input in inference endpoint (medium) — a description of the code/config change or compensating WAF rule plus any test evidence.
- A list of tickets/PRs with links that tracked the fixes.

Can you provide these artifacts (screenshots, config snippets, and ticket links) and any compensating controls you put in place? We aim to close the issues in our tracker by 2026-05-15.

Thanks,
Claire Tremblay
Principal Security Engineer
Acme Corp
[attachment: redacted-pentest-summary-20260428.pdf (application/pdf)]
From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Tremblay <claire.t@acmecorp.com>
Date: Sun, 03 May 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for closure artifacts and compensating controls - Acme pentest findings

Hi Claire —

Appreciate the clear list. We can get you artifacts for the scoped findings. Plan below (will attach items in a follow-up):

- S3 ACL/policy: screenshot of the S3 console (access permissions view) + the bucket policy JSON (redacted where appropriate).
- Inference endpoint: short description of the code-level mitigation and the WAF rule we deployed as a compensating control; include a small regression test log that demonstrates the offending vector is blocked.
- Tickets & PRs: links to our internal Jira and the PRs that implemented the changes.

Timeline: I will assemble the artifacts and share them by EOD Friday 2026-05-07. If you need them sooner for gating a release, let me know and I can prioritize.

Looping in Rishi (security lead) and Marissa from CS for visibility.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request for closure artifacts and compensating controls - Acme pentest findings

Thanks, Soojin. Quick clarifying ask on the S3 item: our notes show the original finding called out an "Unauthenticated GET to artifacts bucket" (Finding 2). Can you show the exact change that prevents public read access? A screenshot of the console is fine, but we need to be able to map it to the steps the pentester cited (ACL vs bucket policy vs public access block).

Also please provide the Jira ticket(s) so the reviewer can validate the change history (who applied it, when).

Appreciate it — we really try to avoid re-testing if the artifacts are clear.

Claire
From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Tremblay <claire.t@acmecorp.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2026 11:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for closure artifacts and compensating controls - Acme pentest findings

Hi Claire — attaching the requested artifacts below and a short summary of the compensating controls we implemented. All attachments are redacted where necessary.

Attachments (sent):
- 20260509-s3-acl-screenshot.png — S3 permissions view showing "Block all public access" toggles enabled and the effective bucket policy shown in the console.
- config-snippet-bucket-policy.txt — redacted bucket policy JSON showing deny for "Principal": "*" on s3:GetObject, with a comment where we removed tester-facing exceptions.
- JIRA-4721-closure-log.txt — export of the Jira ticket (JIRA-4721) showing timeline: ticket opened 2026-04-29, change applied 2026-05-02, deployed 2026-05-03.
- redacted-pentest-summary-20260428.pdf — previously shared; included for context.

Summary of compensating controls and validation:
- Public access: AWS "Block public access" setting was enabled for the account and the bucket policy was tightened to explicitly deny public GetObject. (see config-snippet-bucket-policy.txt)
- Detection: we added an S3 Object-level Lambda that emits an audit log to our central account when a PutBucketAcl/PutBucketPolicy event occurs. Logs are ingested into our SIEM and alert on policy changes.
- Inference endpoint: WAF rule (rule-id waf-2026-11) blocks suspicious payload patterns; we ran a focused regression test suite that shows the vector is rejected (test log attached in JIRA export).

Links:
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/JIRA-4721
- Artifact folder (read-only link): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xYz-example-pentest-artifacts

If you need a raw bucket policy JSON (unredacted) we can provide it under an NDA/secure transfer.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request for closure artifacts and compensating controls - Acme pentest findings

Claire — thanks for the patience. I reviewed the attachments Soojin shared. A couple quick notes from the security team: 

- The screenshot + bucket policy snippet show the public read deny and the account-level public access block — that addresses the specific steps called out in the pentest.
- We recommend keeping the S3 change as permanent, and adding a time-bound alert to the SIEM for any future PutBucketPolicy events that originate outside our change window.

If you want, we can schedule a 20-minute call with our infra engineer to walk through the artifacts and the Jira timeline tomorrow morning.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Security Lead
Redwood Inference
